description.text: Agostino Carracci was born on 16 August 1557 in Bologna as the son of a tailor.  He began his artistic career as a goldsmith before turning to painting, studying under Prospero Fontana and Bartolomeo Passarotti and later travelling to Parma and Venice to absorb the works of Correggio, Veronese and Tintoretto.

Alongside his brother Annibale and cousin Ludovico, Agostino helped found the Accademia degli Incamminati, a progressive school that sought to replace the prevailing Mannerist style with a more naturalistic approach.  He was a prolific reproductive engraver, copying masterpieces of the 16th‑century masters, and also produced original works such as the Communion of St. Jerome, which is regarded as his masterwork.

curiosities.text: He initially trained as a goldsmith before switching to painting.
From 1574 he worked as a reproductive engraver, copying works of Federico Barocci, Tintoretto, Antonio Campi, Veronese and Correggio.
His engraving after Paolo Fiammingo’s Love in the Golden Age later inspired Henri Matisse’s Le bonheur de vivre (Joy of Life).
The Communion of St. Jerome, painted in 1592, is considered his masterwork and was later the subject of a plagiarism accusation by Giovanni Lanfranco against another Carracci student.
